column1: # Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam — Ibn Rajab's preface and the closing lines (the model for the batch translations)

column2: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
And from Him we seek help.

All praise is due to Allah, who perfected the religion for us, completed His favour upon us, made our nation — and to Allah be the praise — the best of nations, and sent among us a Messenger from among ourselves who recites His verses to us, purifies us, and teaches us the Book and wisdom.

I praise Him for His abundant blessings, and I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, without partner — a testimony that will be the best of safeguards for whoever holds fast to it — and I bear witness that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger, whom He sent as a mercy to the worlds and to whom He entrusted the explanation of what was sent down to us;

so he made every important matter clear to us. Allah singled him out with comprehensive words (jawāmiʿ al-kalim), so that he would sometimes gather scattered pieces of wisdom and knowledge into a single phrase, or half a phrase. May Allah send blessings upon him, his family and his Companions — blessings that will be a light for us in every darkness — and grant them abundant peace.
To proceed:
Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, sent Muḥammad ﷺ with comprehensive words and singled him out with remarkable wisdom.
So it is related in the two Ṣaḥīḥs from Abū Hurayrah that the Prophet ﷺ said: “I have been sent with comprehensive words.”

Al-Zuhrī (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Comprehensive words, as we have been told, means that Allah the Exalted gathers for him into one or two statements, or the like, the many matters that used to be written in the books before him.

Imam Aḥmad recorded from the hadith of ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us one day like someone bidding farewell, and said: “I am Muḥammad, the unlettered Prophet.”
He said that three times.
“And there is no prophet after me. I have been given the openings of speech, its conclusions and its comprehensive forms…” and he mentioned the rest of the hadith.

Abū Yaʿlā al-Mawṣilī recorded from the hadith of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet ﷺ said: “I have been given comprehensive words and their conclusions, and speech has been made concise for me.”

Al-Dāraquṭnī (may Allah have mercy on him) recorded from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Prophet ﷺ said: “I have been given comprehensive words, and speech has been made concise for me.”
We have also narrated, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Isḥāq al-Qurashī, from Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I have been given the openings of speech, its conclusions and its comprehensive forms.” We said: O Messenger of Allah, teach us from what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has taught you. And he taught us the tashahhud.
In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from Saʿīd ibn Abī Burdah ibn Abī Mūsā, from his father, from his grandfather: the Prophet ﷺ was asked about bitʿ and mizr [drinks made from honey and from barley],
and — the narrator said — the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been given comprehensive words and their conclusions, so he said: “I forbid every intoxicant that intoxicates one away from the prayer.”

Hishām ibn ʿAmmār related in his book al-Mabʿath, with his chain of narration, from Abū Sallām al-Ḥabashī, who said: I was told that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: “I have been favoured over those before me with six things, and I say it without boasting,”

and among them he mentioned: “I have been given comprehensive words. The People of the Book used to recite them as a portion through the night until morning, and Allah gathered them for me in a single verse: ‘Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise’ [al-Ḥadīd 57:1].”
The comprehensive words with which the Prophet ﷺ was singled out are, then, of two kinds.

The first is what is in the Qurʾān, such as His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: “Indeed, Allah commands justice, excellence and giving to relatives, and forbids indecency, wrongdoing and transgression” [al-Naḥl 16:90]. Al-Ḥasan said:
This verse left no good without commanding it, and no evil without forbidding it.
The second is what is in his own speech ﷺ, and it is found throughout the Sunnah transmitted from him ﷺ.
Scholars have made collections of his comprehensive sayings ﷺ. The ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr ibn al-Sunnī compiled a book he named
al-Ījāz wa-Jawāmiʿ al-Kalim min al-Sunan al-Maʾthūrah, and the judge Abū ʿAbdillāh al-Quḍāʿī gathered concise comprehensive sayings into a book he named

al-Shihāb fī al-Ḥikam wa-l-Ādāb. Others compiled works on the same pattern and added a great deal to what he had mentioned, and al-Khaṭṭābī pointed to a few of the comprehensive hadiths at the beginning of his book Gharīb al-Ḥadīth.

The imam and ḥāfiẓ Abū ʿAmr ibn al-Ṣalāḥ (may Allah have mercy on him) dictated a session he named al-Aḥādīth al-Kulliyyah (“The Universal Hadiths”), gathering in it the comprehensive hadiths of which it is said
that the religion revolves around them, together with concise, comprehensive sayings of similar meaning; that session of his contained twenty-six hadiths.
Then the jurist, imam, ascetic and exemplar Abū Zakariyyā Yaḥyā al-Nawawī (Allah's mercy be upon him) took the hadiths Ibn al-Ṣalāḥ had dictated and added to them until they reached forty-two,

and he named his book al-Arbaʿīn (“The Forty”). These Forty became famous and were widely memorised, and Allah brought benefit through them by the blessing of their compiler's intention and the goodness of his purpose (may Allah have mercy on him).

A number of students of knowledge and religion asked me again and again to write a commentary on these hadiths, so I sought Allah's guidance, Glorified and Exalted is He, about compiling a book that would explain whatever of their meanings Allah the Exalted makes easy,

and set down whatever He, Glorified is He, opens up of their principles and foundations. It is Him I ask for help in what I have set out to do, and for success in keeping my intention and purpose sound. I rely on Him in all my affairs, and I disclaim all might and power except His.

One of those who wrote a commentary on these Forty had faulted their compiler (may Allah have mercy on him) for leaving out the hadith “Give the fixed shares to those entitled to them, and whatever the shares leave over goes to the nearest male relative,” saying

that since it brings together the principles of inheritance, which are half of knowledge, it ought to have been included among these comprehensive hadiths, just as he included the hadith “The burden of proof is on the claimant, and the oath is on the one who denies,” because it brings together the rulings of judgement.

So I decided to add this hadith to the Forty that the Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) compiled, and to add to them all further hadiths from among the comprehensive words that gather different kinds of knowledge and wisdom,
until the hadiths number fifty in all. These are the hadiths added to those the Shaykh (may Allah have mercy on him) gave in his book:

the hadith “Give the fixed shares to those entitled to them”; the hadith “Breastfeeding makes unlawful what lineage makes unlawful”; the hadith “When Allah makes something unlawful, He makes its price unlawful”; the hadith “Every intoxicant is unlawful”; the hadith “No human being fills a vessel worse than his stomach”;

the hadith “There are four traits: whoever has them is a hypocrite”; the hadith “If you relied on Allah as He truly deserves to be relied upon, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds”; and the hadith “Let your tongue remain moist with the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”
I have named it:
Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa-l-Ḥikam fī Sharḥ Khamsīn Ḥadīthan min Jawāmiʿ al-Kalim (“The Compendium of Knowledge and Wisdom: A Commentary on Fifty Hadiths of Comprehensive Words”).

Know that my only aim is to explain the Prophet's words contained in these universal hadiths. For that reason I do not keep to the Shaykh's wording (may Allah have mercy on him) when he introduces the Companions who narrated these hadiths (may Allah be pleased with them),
nor to his wording when he attributes them to the books he cites; I simply give the sense that conveys this,
because, as I have told you, my only aim is to explain the meanings of the comprehensive words of the Prophet ﷺ and the manners, wisdom, knowledge, rulings and laws they contain.
Before explaining each hadith, I briefly indicate its chain of narration,

so that its authenticity, strength or weakness may be known; and I mention some of what has been narrated with the same meaning, if there is anything on the subject besides the hadith the Shaykh gave.

If there is nothing else on the subject, or nothing else on it is authentic, I point all of that out. Allah is the One whose help is sought, upon Him we rely, and there is no might and no power except through Allah.

The end of the book. All praise is due to Allah alone; may Allah send blessings and peace upon our master Muḥammad, his family and his Companions. Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
